newsitem.title: MACAU: Chinese court sentences bank managers to death.
newsitem.headline: Chinese court sentences bank managers to death.

text.p: Two senior Bank of China managers were sentenced to death by a court in China's southern Guangdong province on Wednesday for misappropriating 710 million yuan ($85.6 million) in funds, court officers said.

Section chief Feng Weiquan and deputy section chief Chi Weiqi of the bank's branch in the city of Zhongshan, were given the death penalty by the city's Intermediate People's Court, with Chi's sentence suspended for two years. They have 10 days to appeal.
A judicial source in Zhongshan, 50 km (30 miles) north of the Portuguese territory of Macau, described the case as "the biggest of its kind" since the People's Republic of China was founded in 1949.

The prosecution said the defendants misused a reserve fund of the bank's Great Wall credit card to grant 51 advances to a couple surnamed Chen of the Zhongshan Industrial and Commercial Development Corp between May 1993 and November 1994.
The corporation has since been closed by the Zhongshan municipal government. The whereabouts of the couple were unknown.

Two other defendants, branch director Zheng Daochi and deputy director Cai Hongshang, were sentenced to five years in prison for neglect of duty after being accused of having "lost control" of the bank's credit-card advance-payment services.
